title: Syringe Services Programs
description: 1986. HIV/AIDS is killing thousands. Injection drug users account for 40% of cases. You believe needle exchange can save lives, but it's illegal and politically toxic. Can you prove a controversial harm reduction strategy works?

decisions.title: Underground Beginnings
decisions.contextCard: HIV is spreading rapidly through shared needles. Needle exchange is illegal in most states. Some activists are starting underground programs.

choices.text: Start illegal underground exchange (high risk, immediate impact)
Build coalition first, wait for legal permission

decisions.title: The New Haven Study
decisions.contextCard: Connecticut authorizes a 1-year experimental program in New Haven. This is your chance to prove needle exchange works with rigorous science.

choices.text: Design rigorous evaluation with mathematical modeling
Focus on rapid scale-up, less rigorous evaluation

decisions.title: Breakthrough Results
decisions.contextCard: Your study shows 33% reduction in HIV infections. NYC and multiple cities want to adopt programs. But Congress just banned federal funding for needle exchange.

choices.text: Lobby Congress to overturn the funding ban
Help cities implement with local funds instead

decisions.title: Scientific Consensus
decisions.contextCard: The National Academy of Medicine declares needle exchange reduces HIV without increasing drug use. But political opposition remains fierce.

choices.text: Launch national media campaign with evidence
Work quietly city-by-city to avoid backlash

decisions.title: Slow Growth Era
decisions.contextCard: Programs are spreading despite funding ban. HIV rates are dropping where exchanges operate. Private foundations offer major funding.

choices.text: Accept foundation money to scale rapidly

decisions.title: The Opioid Crisis Arrives
decisions.contextCard: Prescription opioid addiction is exploding. HIV outbreaks are erupting in rural areas with no needle exchanges. This is changing the politics.

choices.text: Pivot to focus on opioid epidemic
Continue urban HIV focus (don't dilute mission)

decisions.title: Indiana Outbreak - Policy Window Opens
decisions.contextCard: Scott County, Indiana: 235 HIV cases in 4 months from opioid injection. Conservative Governor Mike Pence, a needle exchange opponent, is under pressure. This is your moment.

choices.text: Offer immediate technical assistance to Indiana
Demand they follow your model exactly
Wait for federal government to act

decisions.title: Federal Funding Breakthrough
decisions.contextCard: Indiana's success moved Congress. In 2016, federal funds can now support needle exchange operations (but not purchase needles directly). Programs are spreading nationwide.

choices.text: Build national infrastructure for rapid scale-up
Focus on program quality and fidelity
